neutral_facts.value: The accused, a male individual, is alleged to have sexually assaulted his 12-year-old niece. The incident occurred when the victim was asked to sit on the accused's lap, followed by hugging, kissing on the cheeks, and attempts to kiss on the lips. The accused also attempted to disrobe the victim and made lewd comments. The victim, who was an excellent student, experienced trauma that significantly impacted her academic performance. She was taken for counseling, where she eventually disclosed the incident during a second session. A First Information Report (FIR) was registered, and a medical examination was conducted. The victim's statements were recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The accused sought anticipatory bail, which was initially denied by the Sessions Court but later granted by the High Court under certain conditions. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, emphasizing the seriousness of the allegations and the need for the investigation to proceed without interference.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused, being the maternal uncle of the victim, sexually assaulted his 12-year-old niece by hugging, kissing, attempting to disrobe her, and making lewd comments, which caused severe trauma to the victim, impacting her academic performance. The FIR was registered after the victim disclosed the incident during counseling, and the investigation was ongoing.

quotes.text: The victim was traumatized to an extent that she slumped down in her course and performance although she was an excellent student giving good performances
The victim was taken to counselling but did not open up. The victim was taken for second counselling session and at that time, she disclosed the unfortunate incident

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the High Court wrongly granted anticipatory bail, as the Investigating Officer should have free hand to complete the investigation. They also suggested that the delay in reporting the crime and the existence of another FIR might indicate a retaliatory motive.

quotes.text: The Investigating Officer deserves free hand to take the investigation to its logical conclusion
There appears to be a serious misconception of law that if no case for custodial interrogation is made out by the prosecution, then that alone would be a good ground to grant anticipatory bail

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legislative intent of Section 29 of the POCSO Act, which presumes the commission of the offence by the accused unless proven otherwise, and emphasized the importance of the prima facie case in granting anticipatory bail.

quotes.text: The fact that the victim was traumatized to such a high degree that her academic pursuits were adversely impacted alone, coupled with the legislative intent especially reflected through s.29 of the POCSO Act, are sufficient to dissuade a Court from exercising its discretionary jurisdiction in granting pre-arrest bail
The presumption under Section 29 of the Act is not absolute. The statutory presumption would get activated or triggered only if the prosecution proves the essential basic facts
